articles.title: Silicone Upstream-Downstream Tug-of-War in Stalemate, Overall Trading Subdued [SMM Silicone Weekly Review]
articles.description: [SMM Silicone Weekly Review: Stalemate in the tug-of-war between upstream and downstream in the silicone market, overall trading remains subdued] This week, China's silicone market was characterized by a stalemate, with firm cost support and weak end-use demand. Rising prices of upstream raw materials provided strong support for product prices, and enterprises showed sufficient willingness to maintain stable prices. However, downstream end-user follow-through was sluggish, and overall market transactions were mainly driven by restocking for rigid demand. The industry was dominated by a strong wait-and-see sentiment, and price trends across various product categories showed structural divergence.

articles.title: Standard Chartered Received $29 Million From Sale of Cameroon Unit to Access Bank
articles.description: Standard Chartered received $29 million, approximately CFA16.3 billion, from the sale of its Cameroon subsidiary to Access Bank. The amount, which was not disclosed when the transaction closed in December 2025, appears in the British banking group's 2025 financial statements, published on February 24, 2026. In its cash flow statement, Standard Chartered provides a breakdown of the proceeds from three African disposals completed in 2025. Of the $48 million received, $29 million came from the sale of Standard Chartered Bank Cameroon, $13 million from operations sold in Tanzania, and $6 million from its Gambian subsidiary. Note 6 of the financial statements confirms these amounts and specifies that they represent the cash consideration received for the transactions. At the reference exchange rate of December 5, 2025, when the Cameroon transaction was completed, the $29 million was equivalent to approximately CFA16.34 billion. On that date, one euro was worth $1.1645. Based on the fixed exchange rate of CFA655.957 per euro, the dollar amount converts to roughly CFA16.34 billion. This conversion provides an approximate value in CFA francs. It does not necessarily reflect the exchange rate used for accounting purposes when the payment was settled. articles.title: PSEi snaps two-day slide after holding 5,600 support
articles.description: The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) rose on bargain hunting on Thursday, Oct. 15, after the steep drop in the two previous trading days, although investors remained cautious. The main index added 45.94 points, or 0.82 percent, to close at 5,663.17. The property counter posted the biggest gain, while miners and industrials retreated. Volume was higher at 665 million shares worth ₱6.99 billion. Gainers outnumbered losers—91 to 89, with 66 unchanged. “The local index rebounded following two consecutive trading sessions of declines, supported by bargain hunting across the board,” said Regina Capital Development Corp. managing director Luis Limlingan. He noted, though, that “prevailing market sentiment remained cautious as the peso touched the ₱63-to-the-United States (US) dollar level, reflecting continued currency weakness.” Philstocks Financial Inc. research manager Japhet Tantiangco said the local market bounced back as investors picked up shares after the market hit its 5,600 support level. Moving forward, Limlingan said the market is expected to remain wary of economic and geopolitical developments, with investors closely monitoring peso movements and broader macroeconomic conditions.
